items.title: Remove the fixed-length truncation so late-diverging rejection reasons keep distinct digests
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:479 truncates the normalized reason to 200 characters before hashing. ProofStory gap lists share a preamble longer than that, so two different gaps hash identically. Hash the full normalized reason, retaining only a large sanity bound to cap CPU on pathological input.
items.userSees: node packages/main/dist/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.js prints a passing check stating that two real DEV-gate rejection renders differing only past the former 200-character cut produce different digest keys.

happy.desc: gateFailureDigest applied to two reconstructions of the real DEV-gate rejection render (machine.ts:179 preamble plus renderProofStoryDiagnosticReport), identical for their first 244 normalized characters and differing only in the outstanding gap codes, returns two different keys.
The same two rejections routed through bumpGateFailureCount leave maxGateFailureCount at 1, so assessBreaker does not trip, which is the actual operator-visible consequence.

edge.desc: A rejection reason far longer than any realistic gate message still produces a digest, and the retained sanity bound is exercised rather than silently absent.
Two reasons that are identical up to the sanity bound and differ only beyond it are documented as collapsing, so the bound's residual behavior is stated rather than assumed away.

adversarial.desc: Restoring only the fixed-length truncation makes the new smoke assertions fail, proving the check is bound to this change and not to some unrelated property.

verificationEvidence.note: NOT DELIVERED AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN, recorded as such: the C1 class was fixed on main by B-cc54, whose 200-character prefix and signals-fold this branch adopts untouched. What this story delivers of the item is bounded and named: 'must-differ signal-less-long-rejection [guard: signals-conditional-prefix]' widens the prefix when a rejection yields no signals. Recorded by case name and guard tag, no hand-written totals, and as a WHOLE SET — partial re-recording left sibling notes self-contradicting once before (F-045/F-046/F-047).

'must-differ signal-less-long-rejection [guard: signals-conditional-prefix]' drives the real bumpGateFailureCount and asserts the counter consequence, not the hash alone. Mutation M10 (prefix cut made unconditional) fails exactly that case. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

'must-still-collapse scope-extension-proposal-ordinal-past-window [guard: prefix-window-residual]' pins the accepted residual: identical signal sets differing only in a substantive ordinal past the prefix window still collapse, which is what main does too. Measured relaxation bound: mutation M12b (window 200 to 592) fails that case and leaves B-cc54's suite green, while M12 (200 to 600) fails it AND breaks B-cc54's suite at CHK-002:adversarial:1. So a relaxation up to roughly 592 — the measured length of B-cc54's banner fixture — IS available; the window stays at 200 for byte-compatibility with B-cc54, not because no relaxation exists. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

The same residual from the other side: the within-window pair is asserted distinct by 'must-differ scope-extension-proposal-ordinal [guard: substantive-id-whole-token]'. The fixture precondition prints the measured divergence position for both directions, so the bound is pinned rather than described. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

'must-differ proofstory-gap-signal-set [guard: signals-fold]' is this story's guard against silently regressing B-cc54's mechanism: two rejections with identical 200-character prefixes but different non-empty signal sets must digest differently. Mutation M11 (basis collapsed to prefix alone) fails exactly that case. The earlier claim that 'bcc54-cross-vendor-noise' served this purpose was FALSE and is retracted — that case passes under M11 because its fixtures extract no signals. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

items.title: Narrow the path normalizer to machine-specific absolute roots only
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:475 rewrites any slash-bearing token, collapsing DEV/REVIEW with DEV/TEST and src/core/alpha.ts with src/core/beta.ts. Restrict it to absolute paths anchored at machine-specific roots so relative repo paths and slash-bearing identifiers stay distinct while host-varying paths still collapse.
items.userSees: The convergence-breaker smoke prints passing checks stating that DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST digest differently, that two files under a shared first path segment digest differently, and that the same lock path under /Users and under /private/var still digests identically.

happy.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in a slash-bearing identifier (the phase pair DEV/REVIEW versus DEV/TEST) produce different digest keys.
Two rejection reasons naming different repo-relative files under a shared first segment (src/core/alpha.ts versus src/core/beta.ts) produce different digest keys.

edge.desc: The same logical lock path rendered under a machine-specific root (/Users/... versus /private/var/...) still produces one digest key, so host-varying paths keep collapsing.
A path that begins at a machine-specific root but continues into repo-relative segments is normalized once, without leaving a partially-rewritten remainder that could differ per host.

adversarial.desc: Restoring the greedy slash-anchored regex makes the new distinctness checks fail while the machine-path collapse check keeps passing, proving both directions are independently bound to this change.

items.title: Narrow the numeric normalizer to standalone numbers only
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:476 rewrites digit runs inside identifier tokens, collapsing CHK-001 with CHK-002. Restrict it so digits attached to an identifier survive while free-standing counters such as attempt numbers still collapse.
items.userSees: The convergence-breaker smoke prints a passing check stating that a rejection naming CHK-001 and one naming CHK-002 digest differently, alongside a passing check that two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still digest identically.

happy.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in an identifier-embedded ordinal (CHK-001 versus CHK-002) produce different digest keys.

edge.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in free-standing counters and an ISO timestamp still produce one digest key, so genuine retries of one failure keep accumulating.
A story id such as B-bf52, whose digits are attached to an identifier, survives normalization, so rejections naming different stories are not conflated.

adversarial.desc: Restoring the unconditional digit-run rewrite makes the identifier-ordinal distinctness check fail while the free-standing-counter collapse check keeps passing.

verificationEvidence.note: 'must-differ checklist-ordinal', 'finding-ordinal' and 'unfixed-bug-ordinal' [guard: substantive-id-allowlist] assert that an ordinal naming WHICH lifecycle artifact failed survives normalization, printing both compared values literally. 'init-check-issue-ordinal' is deliberately NOT in this group: review showed the init-check issue id is reviewer-self-assigned, overwritten wholesale on every init_check_set and remediated by re-running the reviewer, so it is bookkeeping, and it now sits in must-still-collapse under review-bookkeeping-not-allowlisted. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

'must-still-collapse bare-attempt-ordinal [guard: digit-rule-collapse]' asserts two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still share one key and still trip the brake, matching the frozen userSees. 'lease-heartbeat-age' and 'lane-counts' extend the same direction. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

'must-differ scope-extension-proposal-ordinal [guard: substantive-id-whole-token]' asserts a compound artifact id keeps its trailing ordinal distinct; mutation M6 fails exactly that case. Three cases pin the converse under review-bookkeeping-not-allowlisted — 'stale-review-run-evidence', 'review-loop-ordinal' and 'init-check-issue-ordinal' — because each of those ids is re-minted or retyped on retry, so collapsing is the fail-safe direction for a brake. 'must-still-collapse embedded-test-output-hyphen-compounds [guard: substantive-id-token-start]' guards the regression where a hyphen-joined compound such as de-bug-2 survived normalization because a hyphen creates the very word boundary the old guard relied on. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

Revert-proofs by named mutation, each re-derived from source with the anchor asserted to apply. M7 (allowlist emptied) fails exactly 'checklist-ordinal', 'finding-ordinal', 'unfixed-bug-ordinal' and 'scope-extension-proposal-ordinal'; before the empty-allowlist safety this mutation aborted an earlier assertion and named no case at all. M8 (b- added) fails 'bcc54-story-id-digits' here and CHK-002:adversarial:2 in B-cc54's suite. M9 (rr-/rp-/rl- added) fails the review-bookkeeping cases. M14 (i- re-added) fails exactly 'init-check-issue-ordinal'. M15 (token-start guard weakened to a word boundary) fails exactly 'embedded-test-output-hyphen-compounds'. M13 (numeric placeholder alphabet) fails the same four as M7. M5b (ISO and digit rules both deleted) aborts at a section-7 assertion BEFORE the matrix and names no matrix case — recorded as it behaves, not as a named-subset proof. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). items.title: Extend the convergence-breaker smoke with a substantive-versus-incidental digest matrix
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:180-182 asserts distinct reasons do not accumulate but uses fixtures too short and too plain to reach any collapse rule. Add the four must-differ cases (long-preamble ProofStory gaps, phase pair, checklist ids, in-repo file paths) and the three must-still-collapse cases (timestamps and attempt counters, machine-specific absolute paths, hex digests), each driving the real bumpGateFailureCount and maxGateFailureCount path so the counter consequence is proven, not just the hash.
items.userSees: npm run test:convergence-breaker exits zero and its output lists the must-differ and must-still-collapse digest cases by name, each reporting the resulting gate-failure counter value rather than only the hash.

happy.desc: Every must-differ case drives the real bumpGateFailureCount path twice and then asserts maxGateFailureCount is 1, proving the counter consequence rather than only the hash inequality.
npm run test:convergence-breaker exits zero from a clean build, so the matrix is reachable through the root full test suite that gates DONE.

edge.desc: Every must-still-collapse case drives bumpGateFailureCount twice and asserts maxGateFailureCount reaches 2 and assessBreaker still trips, proving the breaker keeps catching a genuine repeat.
The pre-existing assertions in this smoke, including the reset-clears-counter case, keep passing unchanged alongside the new matrix.

adversarial.desc: Each of the three normalizer changes reverted individually causes a named subset of the matrix to fail and leaves the rest passing, so the matrix localizes which rule regressed instead of failing as one opaque block.

verificationEvidence.note: Every must-differ case prints keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed, each having driven the real bumpGateFailureCount twice and read back maxGateFailureCount and assessBreaker. The suite's closing banner derives its inventory from the case arrays, so a printed count cannot drift from the matrix. Every must-still-collapse case prints keys=1 counter=2 breaker=trips, proving the brake still catches a genuine repeat. The set covers the three machine-path shapes, both B-cc54 fixtures, the three review-bookkeeping ids, the hyphen-compound regression, the past-window residual, bare attempt ordinals, lease heartbeat ages, lane counts, hex ids and ISO timestamps. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). B-cc54's suite is byte-unmodified by this story (git diff main on that path is empty) and exits 0. The completeness guard is BIDIRECTIONAL: it fails naming an UNCLASSIFIED prefix when a scanned producer has no entry, and naming a NO PRODUCER entry when a declared prefix has no producer, so the enumeration drift that caused this story's own errors is now caught by the suite rather than by the next review round. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

Revert-proofs cover every changed rule and both guard directions, each named in the suite output: M1/M2 path rule, M3 digit rule, M4 hex rule, M5a/M5b the ISO-digit redundancy, M6 whole-token, M7/M8/M9/M14 allowlist membership, M10 conditional prefix, M11 signals fold, M12/M12b window widening, M13 placeholder encoding, M15 token-start guard, and G1/G2/G3 for the completeness guard's unclassified, no-producer and broken-citation directions. On the window: M12b (200 to 592) leaves B-cc54's suite green while M12 (200 to 600) breaks it, so widening IS available up to about 592 and 200 is kept for byte-compatibility — the earlier claim that widening was unavailable is withdrawn.
